above.source: 05.2-CONTEXT D-17; the conversion rule for these rows is set in 05.2-07 from the 05.2-06 decision D-35

rule.value: an unknown-price row (its discount unknown: at or below unknown_price.below_or_equal or above unknown_price.above) is converted at the full base price, with no response applied, tagged and counted per run; 'unknown price' means an unknown discount or markdown status, never a missing amount; the money price is the category row's Assumption, and a product whose category row has no price gets no money figure: its financial comparisons are unavailable, and full price never stands in for a missing amount
rule.source: 05.2-06 D-35 (user), definition checked 2026-10-17: the dataset has no money price column and discount is a ratio

full_price.source: dataset card: 1.0 means no discount, 0.9 means 10% off
full_price.note: a known-price row below this is a discounted row

max_bytes_billed.source: user 2026-10-17: the budget limit is enforced on every paid query
max_bytes_billed.note: 5 GiB, about 5 times the roughly 1 GB a query over the 22.1 M-row input reads; every BigQuery query job of the public forecast sets it as maximum_bytes_billed, so BigQuery refuses a query over it without charging, and every paid query is dry-run first and not sent when its estimate is over it (the ARIMA_PLUS training after AI.FORECAST, on the series that need the fallback). The US$30/month billing alert only warns; this cap stops. A run-time guard of the user's BigQuery run, not an input of the set, so public_config.fingerprint leaves this block out
